event.proposal: family: position representation; current retained incumbent is 3136 parameters at 99.9500%, a +0.95 percentage-point margin over 99%. Same-family accepted result: none; same-family failed result: attempt-0026, removing positional vectors at special-token slots while keeping digit positions at 3520/1.06% (with earlier sinusoidal and factorized position trials also failing); prior attempts in this family: 5. Hypothesis: in the reversed fixed layout, operand A and operand B use the same column index and may share one positional vector while their token identities and the plus separator retain role information. Keep every digit-column vector for answer positions, operators, BOS, and EOS distinct, but map B columns 12–21 onto A columns 1–10, reducing the position table from 35 to 25 rows and yielding 2976 parameters. This is more informative than another whole-table low-rank or special-token deletion because it tests only the A/B column symmetry while preserving all answer-column positions; the nearest untested alternative is tying answer columns to operand columns, which removes role distinctions simultaneously. Keep d16/h2/L2, independent head-local maps, MQA, ff16, affine-free block pre-norms, final affine norm, reversed operands, mixed-digit curriculum, and 30000 steps; retain only official accuracy >=99% and strictly below 3136 parameters.
